claims.assertion: The GPS record shows the driver waited stationary for 4 minutes 0 seconds (08:47:55–08:51:55) while on the trip, which is more than the 3-minute wait the policy requires before a driver-side no-show cancellation.

The driver did press the arrival button before cancelling — he tapped it at 08:48:15 and cancelled only at 08:51:55 — so the 'driver must press I'm Here' element of the no-show rule is met on the record as the driver reports it.

The driver's conduct was consistent with a genuine arrival: he messaged the rider 'I'm here already, silver Toyota Altis, please come out' at 08:48 and announced 'Waited more than 3 min, cancelling' at 08:51, i.e. he gave the rider notice and time to come out rather than cancelling immediately.

The $6.61 cancellation fee was charged only because the driver cancelled after the wait the policy contemplates, and it has not been shown to have been levied twice or with any unlisted add-on (surge multiplier 1.0x, no additional fees recorded).

To the extent the fee is upheld, the $6.61 should stand as charged rather than be refunded in full, because the driver-side conditions for a no-show fee are, on the driver's account, satisfied and the rider's own account shows she was present but did not board.

No safety escalation is warranted: there were no traffic incidents or congestion records on the route and the weather was fair, so nothing in the trip window suggests the driver was prevented from reaching the pickup.

weaknesses: The system records contradict the driver's account on the decisive element: F1 shows his closest approach to the pickup was only 288 m and he never came within 200 m, F2 places his 4-minute stop 350 m from the pickup, and F5/F4 show 'I'm Here' tapped 350 m away with 0 s spent inside the 200 m radius and no platform-recorded arrival — under NS-2 that alone defeats the (ii) element and triggers a full $6.61 refund.

The fact index is internally inconsistent about the button: F5 says the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 08:48:15 while F6 says driver_pressed_here_at is null; the rider will rely on F6 to argue the (i) element also fails, and under the system-records-win rule both F5 and F6 outweigh the driver's statement F12.

The chat (F9, F11) is the driver's own outbound notice and the rider's reply 'I don't see any car' (F10) corroborates the rider's version rather than the driver's, so these statements cannot carry the (i)/(ii) elements and, read together with F5, expose the driver to the NS-2 abuse-of-arrival-button flag as well.
Although the driver waited 4 minutes (F2) — enough for element (iii) — NS-2 makes the fee fall away if any element fails, so proving the wait length alone does not save the fee.

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.95)
events.body: The case is a driver-side no-show cancellation: the driver cancelled the trip at 08:51:55 and a $6.61 cancellation fee sits on the record, so the fee can only stand if the NS-1 conditions are all met [F3][F7][NS-0][NS-1]. The first element is satisfied on the face of the records — an "I'm Here" tap is logged at 08:48:15 [F5][NS-1]. However, the location element fails: at the moment of the tap the driver was 350 m from the pickup point, and his closest approach across the whole trip was 288 m, i.e. he never entered the 200 m pickup radius [F1][F5][NS-1]. The waiting element fails likewise: after the tap he spent 0 s continuously inside the radius, and his 4 min 0 s stationary period (08:47:55–08:51:55) was spent 350 m from the pickup point, so a wait "at the pick-up location" is not established even though its duration exceeded 3 minutes [F2][F5][NS-1].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher; record the driver's arrival-button abuse; send the driver account for review (NS-2/RD-6) + flag_account

The first element is satisfied on the face of the records — an "I'm Here" tap is logged at 08:48:15 [F5][NS-1]. However, the location element fails: at the moment of the tap the driver was 350 m from the pickup point, and his closest approach across the whole trip was 288 m, i.e. he never entered the 200 m pickup radius [F1][F5][NS-1]. The waiting element fails likewise: after the tap he spent 0 s continuously inside the radius, and his 4 min 0 s stationary period (08:47:55–08:51:55) was spent 350 m from the pickup point, so a wait "at the pick-up location" is not established even though its duration exceeded 3 minutes [F2][F5][NS-1].

rejected_claims.reason: The 4 min 0 s stationary period is at coordinates 350 m from the pickup point, not at the pickup point, so it cannot satisfy NS-1 (iii) read with NS-1 (ii); duration alone is not enough [F2][F1][NS-1][NS-2].

The tap exists at 08:48:15 but was made 350 m from the pickup point with 0 s subsequently spent inside the 200 m radius, and F6 logs no button press at all; the system records (F4, F5, F6) prevail over the driver's statement, so the arrival element is not established [F5][F6][F4][F12][NS-1][NS-2].

Chat notices cannot substitute for the location requirement; F9 was sent while the driver was 350 m away and the rider's reply says she was at the pickup point and saw no car, which corroborates non-arrival [F9][F10][F2][NS-1][NS-2].

The existence of the fee is not disputed; its lawfulness is. Because NS-1 (ii)/(iii) fail, NS-2 requires the full fee back regardless of whether any add-on or double charge occurred [F7][F1][F5][NS-2].
The rider did not board because the driver was parked 350 m away, not because of a rider no-show; profile history (F16) cannot decide the case and does not save the fee [F2][F10][F16][NS-1][NS-2].

The request for an account flag is upheld, not rejected, but it is grounded in NS-2 (an arrival tap made 350 m outside the pickup area while the driver never came within 200 m), not in RD-6, which concerns route deviation and is inapplicable to this no-show case [F5][F1][NS-2][RD-6].

actions.detail: account action is never automatic; queued for Ryde review

what_would_change: Had NS-1 (ii) held ((ii) within 200 m of pickup AT THE MOMENT of the tap), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.
Had NS-1 (iii) held ((iii) stayed at the pickup > 3 min after the tap, until cancelling), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.

claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: GPS shows his closest approach was 288 m and he never came within 200 m of the pickup, so the NS-1 (ii) location requirement is not met.
The platform's own timeline never records an arrival at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null), which independently confirms no arrival occurred.

The 'I'm Here' tap at 08:48:15 happened while the driver was 350 m from the pickup point and he stayed within 200 m for 0 seconds after the tap, so NS-1 (i)/(ii) fail and the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full.
The driver's 4 minutes of waiting from 08:47:55 to 08:51:55 was spent 350 m away from the pickup point, not at the pickup point, so the NS-1 (iii) waiting condition also fails.

The driver's chat claim that he was 'here already' and then cancelled as a no-show is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records, which under the system-record rule prevail over his statement and his after-the-fact 'I'm Here' claim.
The rider was at the pickup point and asked the driver where he was, corroborating that no no-show by the rider occurred; the $6.61 fee charged at F7 is therefore not payable.

Because the driver pressed 'I'm Here' while GPS placed him outside the pickup area (200 m radius not met), Ryde's fraud rules on abusing the arrival/cancellation button are triggered, so an account flag should accompany the refund.
No traffic incident or congestion record exists on the route during the trip window, so there is no operational explanation excusing the driver's failure to reach the pickup point.

weaknesses: The driver did press 'I'm Here' and did wait about 4 minutes (F5, F2), which on paper resembles the NS-1 waiting pattern; the other side will argue he satisfied the arrival/wait requirements and that the rider simply was not there.

The rider's own 90-day history shows 1 upheld no-show dispute (F16), so the driver may argue the rider is a repeat no-show; this is profile-only and cannot decide the case, but it weakens the credibility framing.
The driver's chat message 'I'm here already' (F9) is a contemporaneous statement the other side will cite, though it is contradicted by the GPS record (F1, F5).
The driver has a clean 90-day record with 689 trips and no disputes (F17), which the other side will use to argue good faith.

claims.assertion: The GPS record shows the driver waited stationary for 4 minutes 0 seconds (08:47:55–08:51:55) while on the trip, which is more than the 3-minute wait the policy requires before a driver-side no-show cancellation.

The driver did press the arrival button before cancelling — he tapped it at 08:48:15 and cancelled only at 08:51:55 — so the 'driver must press I'm Here' element of the no-show rule is met on the record as the driver reports it.

The driver's conduct was consistent with a genuine arrival: he messaged the rider 'I'm here already, silver Toyota Altis, please come out' at 08:48 and announced 'Waited more than 3 min, cancelling' at 08:51, i.e. he gave the rider notice and time to come out rather than cancelling immediately.

The $6.61 cancellation fee was charged only because the driver cancelled after the wait the policy contemplates, and it has not been shown to have been levied twice or with any unlisted add-on (surge multiplier 1.0x, no additional fees recorded).

To the extent the fee is upheld, the $6.61 should stand as charged rather than be refunded in full, because the driver-side conditions for a no-show fee are, on the driver's account, satisfied and the rider's own account shows she was present but did not board.

No safety escalation is warranted: there were no traffic incidents or congestion records on the route and the weather was fair, so nothing in the trip window suggests the driver was prevented from reaching the pickup.

weaknesses: The system records contradict the driver's account on the decisive element: F1 shows his closest approach to the pickup was only 288 m and he never came within 200 m, F2 places his 4-minute stop 350 m from the pickup, and F5/F4 show 'I'm Here' tapped 350 m away with 0 s spent inside the 200 m radius and no platform-recorded arrival — under NS-2 that alone defeats the (ii) element and triggers a full $6.61 refund.

The fact index is internally inconsistent about the button: F5 says the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 08:48:15 while F6 says driver_pressed_here_at is null; the rider will rely on F6 to argue the (i) element also fails, and under the system-records-win rule both F5 and F6 outweigh the driver's statement F12.

The chat (F9, F11) is the driver's own outbound notice and the rider's reply 'I don't see any car' (F10) corroborates the rider's version rather than the driver's, so these statements cannot carry the (i)/(ii) elements and, read together with F5, expose the driver to the NS-2 abuse-of-arrival-button flag as well.
Although the driver waited 4 minutes (F2) — enough for element (iii) — NS-2 makes the fee fall away if any element fails, so proving the wait length alone does not save the fee.

points.response: The 4-minute stationary period at F2 occurred 350 m from the pickup point, not at it; under NS-1(iii) read with NS-1(ii) a wait only counts when the driver is within the pickup area, and F1 confirms he never entered it (closest approach 288 m). Duration alone therefore cannot satisfy NS-1.

The tap at F5 was made 350 m from the pickup point with 0 s subsequently spent inside 200 m, and F6 records no 'I'm Here' tap at all — so on the system records the (i) element fails and the (ii) element fails regardless; F12 (the driver's statement) loses to F4/F5/F6 under the system-records-win rule.

Notice messages cannot substitute for the location requirement: F9 was sent at 08:48 while the driver was 350 m away (F2), and the rider's reply F10 says she was at the pickup point and saw no car, which corroborates non-arrival rather than a genuine arrival under NS-1(ii).

The fee's existence at F7 is not in dispute; its lawfulness is. Because NS-1(i)(ii) fail on F1/F4/F5/F6, NS-2 requires the full $6.61 to be refunded — no double-charge or add-on issue is needed to reach that result.

This restates D1–D3 and ignores F2's own coordinates: the rider 'did not board' because the driver was parked 350 m away, and F10 shows she was at the pickup point waiting, so the rider-side element of NS-1 is not met and NS-2 applies.

Agreed that no safety escalation is needed; the rider seeks no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation. Traffic (F13, F14) and weather (F15) simply confirm there was no impediment excusing the failure to reach the pickup point, which supports NS-2 rather than the driver.
Narrowing C6: the chat reply F10 is user-submitted and loses to the GPS/timeline records; the refund rests on F1/F4/F5/F6 (system records), with F10 only as context.

Maintaining the flag request: F5 records an 'I'm Here' tap 350 m outside the pickup area while F1 shows he never came within 200 m, which is exactly the NS-2 abuse-of-arrival-button scenario; the request is supported additionally, not solely, by the driver profile F17.
Conceded on the record: F1 puts the closest approach at 288 m, outside the 200 m arrival radius, so the NS-1 (ii) location element is not established and the fee falls under NS-2.
Conceded: F4 shows driver_arrived_at is null, so the platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point, which is corroborating evidence the rider is entitled to rely on under NS-2.

Conceded in part: although F5 shows the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 08:48:15, F5 also records 350 m from the pickup and 0 s inside the 200 m radius, so element (ii) fails and the $6.61 falls away under NS-2 — but on F7 alone the amount refundable is exactly $6.61, no more.

Partially contested: F2 does establish a 4 min 0 s wait and F3 confirms the cancel at 08:51:55 (7 min 55 s after acceptance), so element (iii) is met and the failure is purely one of location under NS-1 (ii), not of waiting.
Conceded: the driver's chat claim F9/F11/F12 cannot carry the arrival element because the system records F1 and F5 contradict it, and system records prevail.

Not contested on outcome: F10 shows the rider at the pickup point and the driver never reached it (F1), so the $6.61 at F7 is refundable in full under NS-2 — the rider's remedy is the voucher the policy prescribes, and NS-7 caps it at that amount.

Contested to the extent it matters for my client: an account flag is an additional action under NS-2, and the rider cannot get two remedies for one $6.61 fee, so the outcome should be the single refund_full of $6.61 without duplicating relief; RD-6 is a route-deviation clause, not applicable to a no-show case.

Accepted as accurate but immaterial: F13, F14 and F15 merely show no traffic or weather excuse existed, which my case never asserted, so they add nothing beyond the location failure already conceded at C1.
Withdrawn: F2 shows the wait length but F2 also places the stop 350 m from the pickup, so under NS-2 the 4-minute wait cannot satisfy the combined NS-1 test once the location element fails.

Withdrawn so far as it sought to preserve the fee: the driver asked for no_action, but the record at F1/F4/F5 makes NS-2 refund_full the correct outcome, and the rider's profile F16 is irrelevant to that computation under NS-2.
Stands unchanged: F13, F14 and F15 confirm no safety or traffic escalation is needed, which remains true and simply leaves the NS-2 refund as the whole of the case.
